title: Trump’s State Department Is Giving $1 Million to Controversial Group to Study Crimes Against White South Africans
author: Anna Maria Barry-Jester
content:
After slashing funding for programs that documented atrocities and protected
human rights abroad, President Donald Trump’s State Department is now granting
one of its first new human rights awards to a controversial South African
organization that promotes the disputed notion that white farmers are a
violently targeted, persecuted group, according to multiple sources
knowledgeable about the funding.

The group expected to receive the nearly $1 million award, AfriForum, is a
nonprofit that advocates on behalf of Afrikaners, a subset of South Africa’s
white population. The organization says its members, who have a “[God-given
calling](https://afriforum.co.za/en/about-us/),” fight for Afrikaner interests
and self-governance. The money will be used to “[document hateful rhetoric and
violent acts](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-democracy-human-rights-
and-labor/2026/08/documentation-of-hateful-rhetoric-targeting-minority-
populations-in-south-africa)” against Afrikaners and other minority
populations in the country.

The new award comes from a State Department bureau tasked with promoting
democracy and human rights internationally. Until last year, those funds were
mainly spent in poor and authoritarian nations — to fight corruption in the
Democratic Republic of Congo, for example, or combat child exploitation and
sexual abuse in Afghanistan. Since Trump returned to office, his appointees
have transformed the bureau, gutting its staff, canceling programs and
reorienting some of its funding toward conservative causes in Europe.

Samuel Samson, who was appointed as a deputy assistant secretary to the State
Department bureau by Trump, has claimed the U.S. [has a “civilizational”
connection](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1FDedZCs-6c) to Afrikaners, who
descend primarily from Dutch migrants and predominantly speak Afrikaans.
Samson, who has met with far-right leaders in Europe since joining the
administration last year, has framed the U.S. government’s financial support
for Afrikaners as grounded in “a common heritage, a common culture, a common
way of life, shared history and ultimately a common anthropology.”

### Samuel Samson Speaks at Lex Libertas Event

Samson, left, deputy assistant secretary of state in the Bureau of Democracy,
Human Rights and Labor, is interviewed by Ernst Roets during a Lex Libertas
press conference. Lex Libertas via YouTube

There’s a long shared political history between Afrikaner groups and white
nationalists in the U.S., said Audie Klotz, a political science professor at
Syracuse University who has studied those connections. But, she said, “There’s
no heritage connection here. It’s pure scientific racism. In the history of
U.S. immigration, there’s no direct connection between South Africa and the
United States.”

AfriForum met with the Trump administration in February 2025 to plead for
help. The group told officials that Afrikaners are subject to racial
discrimination and murders that are more frequent and asked the administration
to “act strongly against hate speech that incites violence” against them,
[according to a statement](https://afriforum.co.za/en/washington-memorandum/).

South Africa is plagued by high rates of violence, and some Afrikaners have
been tortured and murdered. But [independent researchers have
found](https://issafrica.org/iss-today/violent-crime-and-the-myth-of-south-
africa-s-white-genocide) those killings represent a tiny fraction of murders
across the country, whose victims are disproportionately people living in poor
urban areas, where residents are predominantly Black. [Official government
statistics](https://dirco.gov.za/south-african-government-sets-record-
straight-on-farm-crime/), and two formal inquiries into the matter, do [not
reveal a pattern](https://crimehub.org/analysis/research/farm-attacks-in-
south-africa-setting-the-record-straight) of targeted violence against
Afrikaners.

But Trump subscribes to the idea that white farmers [face a
“genocide”](https://www.whitehouse.gov/videos/potus-on-south-africa-its-a-
genocide/) and has cited disproportionate violence against them as a reason
for punishing Africa’s wealthiest nation. In February 2025, he [issued an
executive order](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-
actions/2025/02/addressing-egregious-actions-of-the-republic-of-south-africa/)
that cut off hundreds of millions of dollars of aid to South Africa and
welcomed Afrikaners to the U.S. as refugees. Since then, the administration
has [opened the doors to more than 16,000 white South
Africans](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/16/trump-white-south-africans-refugee-
admissions-2026) while halting virtually all other immigration. Officials
recently told Congress they plan to invite [as many as 17,500 Afrikaner
refugees](https://apnews.com/article/refugees-trump-immigration-white-south-
africans-3453e6b9c88104d41274d0ab19e79651) to the U.S. in 2027.

AfriForum did not respond to specific questions for this story but said that
“our understanding is that the allocation has not yet been finalised. Should
the allocation indeed be awarded to AfriForum, we will make a public
announcement in this regard.”

The new award is the administration’s latest show of support for the Afrikaner
cause. The white South African group governed the nation for decades under a
brutal system of segregation known as apartheid, which kept the Black majority
an impoverished underclass until the system was dismantled in 1994. Now, with
Black South Africans governing the country, white people — of which Afrikaners
are the majority — remain one of the wealthiest segments of the population.

The support has caused dismay among several former high-level diplomats, who
spoke to ProPublica anonymously because they fear retribution from the
administration.

![A woman is surrounded by children of different ages. A young girl to the
woman’s left holds a small American flag in her hand and looks directly at the
camera.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/GettyImages-2214742382.jpg?w=2560)Newly arrived South
Africans at Washington Dulles International Airport in 2025. Chip
Somodevilla/Getty Images

Two former senior U.S. officials responsible for Africa policy said that they
would never have met with AfriForum, let alone funded the group, because it
was considered to be politically extreme and not credible. They described the
organization as cherry-picking crime statistics to create a misleading
narrative. “We would certainly not have funded what we would see as a racially
incendiary initiative,” said one of the officials.

The decision to direct money toward the group comes after the Trump
administration halted programs that advocated for the end of violence in
African countries such as Sudan, where the Biden administration [determined in
2025 that there was a genocide](https://2021-2025.state.gov/genocide-
determination-in-sudan-and-imposing-accountability-measures/), calling it “the
world’s largest humanitarian catastrophe.”

“It's offensive to provide funding solely to this one group after we’ve cut
off funding in countries undergoing real documented crises,” said David
Jandura, who managed the Africa portfolio for the State Department’s human
rights bureau for several years and lost his job during the mass layoffs in
2025.

Congress has also raised questions about how the award was made. A Senate aide
to Democrats told ProPublica that despite repeated requests to State
Department officials, they had not received a briefing outlining the
recipients of funds earmarked for democracy and human rights, which they
described as “highly unusual.”

“The Trump Administration proceeded with funding fringe right-wing causes
internationally despite objections from Congress,” said Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, a
New Hampshire Democrat and ranking member of the Senate Committee on Foreign
Relations, who described the lack of transparency as “unacceptable.”

In response to a series of questions about the AfriForum funding, a senior
State Department official wrote in an email that the department does not
comment on funding deliberations and that they routinely keep Congress
informed of their actions, consulting extensively on this year’s programming.
“The Administration has been clear about its concern about the abhorrent race-
based discrimination and violence in South Africa,” the unnamed official
wrote. “Human rights protections do not depend on a person’s income or
ethnicity.”

In July, [ProPublica revealed](https://www.propublica.org/article/human-
rights-aid-right-wing-causes) that the State Department originally intended to
give the $1 million research award to Lex Libertas, a small organization
founded last year by a former AfriForum executive named Ernst Roets. Trump
officials later expanded the potential awardees to a small pool of handpicked
organizations. The plan drew outrage from Congress over the content of the
award as well as plans to bypass the typical competitive bidding process.
After ProPublica’s reporting, the State Department [released an open call for
the funding opportunity](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-democracy-
human-rights-and-labor/2026/08/documentation-of-hateful-rhetoric-targeting-
minority-populations-in-south-africa), offering $986,500 to a nonprofit
organization to “create a comprehensive record of violence affecting Afrikaner
and other South African minority populations.” It’s this grant that is now
being awarded to AfriForum.

Both AfriForum and Lex Libertas advocate for Afrikaner rights and have
developed relationships with the Trump administration. Trump’s ambassador to
South Africa, L. Brent Bozell III, visited AfriForum’s headquarters in
September, [praising the
organization](https://x.com/USAmbRSA/status/2102810594533372339) for its
[neighborhood watch
programs](https://www.artikels.afriforum.co.za/en/afriforums-neighbourhood-
and-farm-watches-simulate-farm-attack-and-hostage-release/) while criticizing
the South African government for not enacting policies requested by the Trump
administration. AfriForum has also met with Trump officials [in Washington,
D.C.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RwYLM5O3NVk), [drawing public
criticism](https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-trump-afrikaner-aid-
freeze-c93da366d91ec386adf99099441cf565) from South African President Cyril
Ramaphosa. And in September, Roets met with administration officials.

AfriForum was founded 20 years ago and, with some 300,000 members, [claims to
be](https://www.artikels.afriforum.co.za/en/afriforum-the-largest-civil-
rights-organisation-in-the-country-celebrates-20-years-of-community-building/)
the biggest civil rights organization in South Africa. It says it aims to
“establish self-dependence and growing self-governance” and provides some
local civic services, such as garbage collection and systems for reporting pot
holes and [broken traffic
lights](https://www.artikels.afriforum.co.za/en/traffic-lights-out-of-order/).
The group has said it distances itself from “white supremacist and extremist
groups” and that it [disagrees with Trump’s
assertion](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1265449608327323) that white South
African farmers are [experiencing a “white
genocide.”](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1265449608327323) But it has also
said the South African government is “[targeting the continued existence of
Afrikaners](https://www.artikels.afriforum.co.za/en/solidarity-movement-
announces-its-five-answers-to-us-asks/)” through racial legislation and the
downplaying of farm murders, among other things. Academics and former U.S.
diplomats have repudiated some of the ideas the group promotes as racist.

![A group of men in khaki pants and black shirts stand in a circle in a field
at night in front of a line of parked vehicles. One of them is pointing at
something behind him, while the others look
on.](https://www.propublica.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/AP25130598283950.jpg?w=2560)Members of AfriForum
assemble before a neighborhood patrol near Pretoria, South Africa, in 2025.
Alet Pretorius/AP Photo

It unsuccessfully challenged a ban on the [“gratuitous display” of the
national flag](https://www.nelsonmandela.org/news/entry/media-statement-no-
more-gratuitous-displays-of-the-apartheid-flag-equality-court) flown during
apartheid, which a South African court has found to be a form of hate speech.
And while the group’s leader, Kallie Kriel, has said apartheid “[was
wrong](https://www.polity.org.za/article/apartheid-was-not-a-crime-against-
humanity-afriforum-ceo-2018-05-14),” he has also said it did not constitute
“[a crime against
humanity](https://www.timeslive.co.za/politics/2018-05-15-uproar-over-remark-
that-apartheid-was-not-a-crime-against-humanity-by-afriforum-ceo/)” as the
[U.N. has determined](https://legal.un.org/avl/ha/cspca/cspca.html), on the
grounds that not enough people were killed during that time.

AfriForum has been focusing on farm attacks since at least 2009. In 2018,
during Trump’s first presidency, Kriel and Roets, who was then his deputy, met
with government officials in Washington, D.C., about the issue, and Roets
spoke about it with [Tucker Carlson on Fox
News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9dMYhLZb96Q), as the chyron below him
announced in all caps, “White farmers brutally murdered every week in
SouthAfrica.”

Additional research on crimes against white South Africans is an unnecessary
and confusing  use of U.S. taxpayer dollars, said Carolyn Holmes, a professor
at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, who studies democracy in southern
Africa. Holmes noted that AfriForum already [produces annual
reports](https://www.artikels.afriforum.co.za/en/afriforum-reports/) on crimes
against farming communities. “These data already exist,” she said. “You don’t
need a new study. You don’t even need a far-right study, we have those.”  

The U.S. support offers more than a financial boost to the organization. “For
some time, AfriForum has been campaigning for recognition of their claim that
white people face discrimination and persecution,” said Alex Dyzenhaus, a
lecturer in international relations and African politics at the University of
St. Andrews. “Before, they were only getting the Tucker Carlsons and the far
right of the news ecosystem. Now they have the U.S. government on their side.”

The Trump administration has made the plight of white, rural South Africans a
key foreign policy issue. In addition to the early executive order, Trump held
a contentious meeting with Ramaphosa in the White House last year where Trump
claimed white farmers were being executed. The administration has also
considered [an ad campaign](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2026/oct/15/us-officials-ad-campaign-south-africa-afrikaners-refugees)
focused on encouraging more Afrikaners to come to the U.S.

[In September, Roets of Lex Libertas met with the White
House](https://www.lexlibertas.org.za/media/lex-libertas-meets-with-white-
house-to-discuss-solutions-for-south-africa-s-political-crisis) to discuss
what he sees as the crisis facing the Afrikaner community and, along with the
New York Young Republican Club, placed [3,000 white crosses on the National
Mall](https://www.lexlibertas.org.za/campaigns/white-cross-project) to
commemorate South African farm murders.

Roets declined to answer specific questions from ProPublica but, in a text
message, described the murders of several Afrikaners that he knew personally.
He also wrote, “I see the suffering of black people in South Africa, I am
deeply moved by it, and I spend every day of my life campaigning to make
things better for us all.”

[Appearing at a press conference](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1FDedZCs-6c)
for the Lex Libertas event, Samson, the State Department official, showcased
the sharp shift the administration has made in U.S. relations with South
Africa. While apartheid has been understood globally as a symbol of racist
oppression, Samson described the current South African government as having
discriminatory “race-based” policies and a cautionary tale for the rest of the
world.  

At the end of apartheid, in 1994, South Africa was a “flourishing, prosperous
society,” Samson said. Since then, the country has gone to “ruin.” He blamed
the fall on a “radical ideological leftist movement that wears human rights,
that wears tolerance and inclusivity, as a skin suit to advance their Marxist
communist worldview.”

Part of the Trump administration’s solution to this perceived crisis, he said,
was to provide the research funding.

The post [Trump’s State Department Is Giving $1 Million to Controversial Group
to Study Crimes Against White South
Africans](https://www.propublica.org/article/afriforum-grant-trump-white-
south-africans) appeared first on [ProPublica](https://www.propublica.org).
